key_insight: A physics-grounded digital twin combining weld-pool simulation and Gaussian-process surrogates shows promise for screening robotic welding conditions and control strategies before in-space joining experiments.
engineering_relevance: Fast surrogate predictions could help adapt welding settings to robot speed changes and reduce the experimental burden of developing reliable on-orbit metal joining.
method: Finite-volume thermal model includes phase change, effective thermocapillary transport, and local pressure; gravity is assessed separately.
Gaussian-process and neural-network surrogates are compared using repeated five-fold cross-validation.
A simulated UR5 follows an L-shaped seam while proportional control adjusts the power-source setting.
evidence_signal: The GP outperformed the neural network on all eight outputs, covered 74/80 held-out solver responses within nominal 90% predictive intervals, and enabled 12/12 closed-loop versus 9/12 open-loop points to meet an illustrative weld-width band in simulation.
watch_item: Results remain simulation-based; thermal-vacuum, reduced-gravity, and robotic hardware-in-the-loop tests are needed to assess model and controller validity.
paper_title: De-Risking Robotic Welding for In-Space Metal Joining Through Physics-Grounded Digital Twins
